newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania plans new forex liberalisation moves.
newsitem.headline: Romania plans new forex liberalisation moves.

text.p: Romania's central bank (BNR) governor Mugur Isarescu on Friday pledged to take new steps to liberalise the foreign exchange market and give individuals the right to exchange more than a present $500 a year.
"We hope we'll be able to abandon the $500 limit on individuals' exchanges later this year," Isarescu told a news conference.
Under current rules Romanians are compelled to limit their hard currency buyings to up to the equivalent of $500 annualy.

The planned move follows a BNR step in February to remove foreign exchange market curbs imposed by the former leftist government in 1996. The BNR restored dealer status to 24 banks to act as market makers along with the existing four dealers.
"We consider last month's move the key to a full liberalisation of the foreign exchange market. But there are still few restrictions to be eliminated," Isarescu said.
He said that rules by the State Ownership Fund -- the major holder of state companies -- imposing that state firms resort only to state-run banks for their operations would also be abolished soon.
"We want our market to operate normally on the long term, which will be the utmost incentive to foreign investors, amounting to all the facilities designed to attract them to Romania," said Isarescu.

Foreign investments in Romania, East Europe's second largest market after Poland, is $2.2 billion or about a tenth of what neighbouring Hungary has attracted over the past seven years since the fall of communism.
Isarescu said the foreign exchange market had turned liquid and "very active" after more than a year a lethargy, while the leu had recently stabilised at around 7,000 to the dollar.
The leu stabilisation followed a slump to 9,000 immediately after curbs had been removed.
"We couldn't get a soft landing as the move triggered large fluctuations (of the exchange rate) but we are past that shock now," he said.
Banks' screen quotes continued to show wide ranges of leu-dollar quotes and spreads between 6,200/7,100 to 6,900/9,500 over the past weeks.

Vice-governor Vlad Soare acknowledged during the same news conference that some spreads were huge triggering a "sort of segmentation of the market" but he said he hoped the problem would be solved in the coming months.
"This is an older disease of this market, which will hopefully be treated in time," Soare said.
Dealers said the leu traded near 6,900 to the dollar on Friday, with the market rather dormant ahead of the weekend.
